description: Na₄Mg(FeO₃)₂ crystallizes in the monoclinic Cm space group. There are two inequivalent Na sites. In the first Na site, Na is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to four O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.22-2.46 Å. In the second Na site, Na is bonded in a 5-coordinate geometry to five O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.32-2.66 Å. Mg is bonded to five O atoms to form distorted MgO₅ trigonal bipyramids that share corners with two FeO₄ tetrahedra and edges with two FeO₄ tetrahedra. There are a spread of Mg-O bond distances ranging from 2.11-2.13 Å. There are two inequivalent Fe sites. In the first Fe site, Fe is bonded to four O atoms to form FeO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two equivalent FeO₄ tetrahedra,  a cornercorner with one MgO₅ trigonal bipyramid, and  an edgeedge with one MgO₅ trigonal bipyramid. There are a spread of Fe-O bond distances ranging from 1.89-1.96 Å. In the second Fe site, Fe is bonded to four O atoms to form FeO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two equivalent FeO₄ tetrahedra,  a cornercorner with one MgO₅ trigonal bipyramid, and  an edgeedge with one MgO₅ trigonal bipyramid. There are a spread of Fe-O bond distances ranging from 1.90-1.96 Å. There are four inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded in a 5-coordinate geometry to three Na, one Mg, and one Fe atom. In the second O site, O is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to four Na, one Mg, and one Fe atom. In the third O site, O is bonded in a 5-coordinate geometry to two equivalent Na, one Mg, and two Fe atoms. In the fourth O site, O is bonded in a tetrahedral geometry to two equivalent Na and two Fe atoms.
